name: Open-Meteo weather forecasts
description: Fetch-plan and normalization nodes for attributed hourly Open-Meteo point forecasts (typed contracts 1.0). plan_forecast turns a TimerTick into ONE HttpRequest whose CONTEXT is the plan as one size-prefixed $WXF header record (source name, 1x1 requested location, canonical URL, licence, producer peer id); parse_forecast turns the HttpResponse (CONTEXT echoed, RETRIEVED_MS the host's retrieval time) into a size-prefixed $WXF stream, ONE IngestRequest for hostcap/storage-ingest (reconcile Current, batch = SHA-256 of the response body) and FlowNotice reports. Node CONFIG through plugin.getConfig (one ModuleConfig, read by dotted path): open_meteo_forecast.latitude / .longitude (numbers), .forecast_days (integer 1-16, default 3), .access (noncommercial | customer, required), .variables.<i> (1-8 supported hourly variables; default temperature_2m, relative_humidity_2m, cloud_cover, wind_speed_10m, pressure_msl, precipitation); open_meteo_producer_peer_id (the daemon's peer id, stamped on every record). The only host call is plan_forecast's builtin plugin.getConfig (SDS $PIV); parse_forecast is pure; no capabilities. No JSON between modules (the upstream body is Open-Meteo's JSON, parsed here).

sequentialJustification.detail: Bounded deterministic point-forecast request planning (one builtin plugin.getConfig hostcall) and pure binary normalization. No threads or network access.

acceptedTypeSets.description: TimerTick (module-sdk runtime type TICK); its payload is not read.

inputPorts.description: The scheduling tick (forwarded by open-meteo-host prepare_scheduled); a direct invoke may send none.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpRequest (HREQ): GET of the canonical forecast URL, TIMEOUT_MS 20000, MAX_BYTES 4 MiB; CONTEXT the plan, one size-prefixed $WXF header record. No credential: a customer API key is attached privately by the host, never in the plan.

methods.description: Reads the forecast plan from node CONFIG and emits ONE HttpRequest carrying the plan ($WXF header) in its CONTEXT. Invalid configuration is refused with a named error and no output.

acceptedTypeSets.description: HttpResponse (HRSP) from hostcap/http-request: STATUS, BODY (Open-Meteo JSON, at most 4 MiB), CONTEXT the plan $WXF header, RETRIEVED_MS.

inputPorts.description: The forecast response; exactly one frame per invocation.

acceptedTypeSets.description: Size-prefixed $WXF stream, one 1x1 field per variable and UTC valid time.

outputPorts.description: Size-prefixed binary WXF stream, one 1x1 field per variable and UTC valid time.

acceptedTypeSets.description: IngestRequest (INGQ): SCHEMA WXF.fbs, TAGS (provider open-meteo, source forecast/<lat>,<lon>, BATCH_ID = SHA-256 of the body, SOURCE_URL, SOURCE_PEER the producer peer, CC-BY-4.0 licence and citation), RECONCILE Current.

outputPorts.description: The batch's ingest request for hostcap/storage-ingest.

acceptedTypeSets.description: FlowNotice (FNTC): Info (COUNT records, AT_MS retrieval time) and, when any sample was null, Missing (COUNT missing samples).

outputPorts.description: What the pass normalized; never a dataset record.

methods.description: Validates the complete response against the plan in its CONTEXT (canonical URL, UTC, unixtime, every requested day and variable, units, sanity bounds; the forecast must start on the retrieval date) and only then emits the records, the IngestRequest and the report. A non-200, a partial or wrong-unit body, or a non-canonical plan is refused with a named error and no output, so the previous dataset stays.
